met_analysis:
The very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” [Pronunciation :Ornab] over Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestwards with a speed of 18 kmph during past 6 hours, and lies centered at 1430 hrs IST of today, the 27th October, 2026 over the same region near latitude 16.2°N and longitude 83.3°E, about 140 km southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 170 km south of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 230 km east of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 300 km east-northeast of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh), and 380 km south- southwest of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to move nearly west-northwestwards during next few hours, then northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to south of Yanam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026.
The trough from southwest Bay of Bengal off Sri Lanka coast to cyclonic circulation associated with the very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” over Westcentral Bay of Bengal extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over south Andaman Sea and neighbourhood & extends upto 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Haryana over northwest Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists. Another Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 73°E to the north of Lat. 28°N persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Uttar Pradesh & adjoining Bihar p at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
